newsitem.title: THAILAND: Foreign bank upgrades look to niches for business.
newsitem.headline: Foreign bank upgrades look to niches for business.

text.p: The seven foreign banks which on Thursday won Thai government approval to upgrade to full branch status hope to use their international expertise and develop existing contacts to compete with onshore lenders.

The banks operating under the Bangkok International Banking Facility were previously allowed only to lend funds to corporate clients. The upgrade will allow them to expand services to provide most of what is available from local banks.
Representatives of some of the banks told Reuters the upgrading will give them the opportunity to expand operations to provide services required by their clients.
Rapeepat Rerkasem, senior vice president at Banque Nationale de Paris, said the bank will use its international network to compete with strong Thai banks.
"We are international banks. So we have more channels than local banks to serve the clients," he said.
Dresdner Bank AG country manager Vichai Punpocha said the upgrade will help its clients invest in Thailand and its neighbouring countries.

"We have a large German customer base interested in directly investing in Thailand," Vichai said. "The major German chemical and pharmaceutical giants have decided to use Thailand as their gateway to Indochina and we aim to offer a full range of services for them."

The seven whose representative offices were upgraded were the Bank of Nova Scotia, Dresdner Bank AG, The Dai-chi Kangyo Bank Ltd, The Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd, The Sumitomo Bank Ltd, Bank of China and Banque Nationale de Paris.
